newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Green candidate loses Stuttgart mayor race.
newsitem.headline: German Green candidate loses Stuttgart mayor race.

text.p: A candidate from the Greens party narrowly lost his bid on Sunday to become the first mayor from the environmentalist party elected to govern a major German city, German network ZDF said.
ZDF forecast that Greens candidate Rezzo Schlauch would receive 40 percent of the vote compared to 43 percent for Wolfgang Schuster, the Christian Democratic (CDU) candidate.
With about half of the ballots counted, election officials in Stuttgart said Schlauch was trailing Schuster by 43.6 percent to 38.1 percent.

ZDF said Schauch had received nearly 60 percent of the vote from those under 40 years old while Schuster had only managed to poll 28 percent of that age group. But Schuster was twice as strong in the older age groups.
Schlauch's second place finish in the first round of voting on October 20 unexpectedly knocked out the Social Democratic (SPD) candidate Rainer Brechtgen, who finished third.
With 600,000 citizens, Stuttgart, state capital of Baden-Wuerttemberg and home to the huge industrial group, Daimler-Benz AG, is Germany's seventh largest city.
The race was to find a successor for Manfred Rommel of the CDU who is retiring after 22 years in the post.

Political analysts had said that even though Schlauch had led in opinion polls the final results could be distorted because of the late wildcard entry into the run-off of Joachim Becker (SPD), who is mayor of the suburban town of Pforzheim.
But Becker received just three percent of the vote, ZDF said.
